summary.text: 场 is the simplified counterpart of 場. The traditional character combines 土, which contributes a ground-related meaning, with 昜 as a sound component. 場 is recorded for ritual ground, grain-working ground, and broader places.

formation.text: The traditional graph 場 is a phonosemantic compound: 土 contributes a ground-related meaning, while 昜 supplies the sound. 场 is its simplified counterpart; the specific graphic route from 場 to 场 remains unresolved.

components.text: In 場, 土 contributes the ground-related semantic category.
In 場, 昜 serves as the phonetic component. Interpretations of its own early graphic origin differ; that question is separate from its sound role here.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Old Chinese system, 昜 (*laŋ) and 場 (*l'aŋ) share the rhyme and syllable shape, though their reconstructed initials differ. In Middle Chinese rhyme-dictionary records, both belong to the 陽 rhyme, while Baxter transcriptions of their readings are yang for 昜 and drjang for 場. These reconstructions and transcriptions represent scholarly analyses, not direct recordings of ancient speech.
sound.system: Old Chinese: Zhengzhang Shangfang; Middle Chinese: rhyme-dictionary categories and Baxter transcriptions

history.text: 場 is analyzed as 土 plus 昜, with 昜 as the sound component. A small-seal form is listed, but the cited records do not establish an oracle-bone or bronze form of 場.
塲 is recorded as a variant of 場. It is distinct from the simplified form 场.
场 is the simplified counterpart of 場. A proposed derivation from cursive writing has not been verified, so the precise graphic route remains unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The earliest surviving attestation of 場 has not been dated here, and no oracle-bone or bronze form is established. A listed small-seal image could not be inspected.
The specific graphic route from 場 to 场, including the proposed cursive derivation, remains unresolved.
The early graphic interpretation of 昜 is debated, independently of its supported phonetic role in 場.

senses.text: An early dictionary account describes 場 as a way or ground for sacrificing to spirits; another interprets it as level ground used for ancient sacrifice. The first surviving occurrence is not dated here.
An early dictionary account also gives 田不耕, an uncultivated field, as an alternative gloss. Its timing relative to the ritual-ground sense is unresolved.

senses.gloss: ground for processing or drying grain
senses.text: A further gloss describes ground for grain processing, and cited texts use 場 for a grain-drying or threshing floor. The evidence does not establish when this use arose relative to the other early glosses.
Textual examples record 場 for a general place and other venues. Modern glosses include open space, field, and market, but neither their order nor their semantic links is established here.
A figurative use meaning a domain is recorded, but its date and development from a physical-place sense are unresolved.
Classifier use is recorded, but its date and development from another sense are unresolved.

developments.text: Both senses are recorded, but a direct development from ritual ground to grain-working ground is not established.
Both grain-working-ground and general-place uses are attested, but the evidence does not establish that one developed from the other.
The figurative domain may extend the physical-place sense metaphorically, though the transition itself is not documented.
Classifier use is attested, but whether or how it developed from the place sense is unresolved.

limitations.text: The cited textual uses are not individually dated, so they do not provide a full semantic chronology or establish the first surviving occurrence.
The evidence supports a 土-plus-昜 phonosemantic construction; it does not support borrowing the entire graph 場 for an unrelated word.

overview.text: 场 is the simplified counterpart of 場. In 場, 土 points to ground and 昜 supplies the sound. The traditional character is recorded for ritual and grain-working grounds, as well as broader places.

components.text: 土 points to earth or ground in the traditional character’s construction.
昜 supplies the sound cue in 場; debate about its own early graphic origin does not change this role.

relationships.text: 土 contributes the ground-related semantic category in traditional 場.
昜 serves as the phonetic component in traditional 場; the cited sound records support a rhyme and syllable-shape correspondence.
场 is identified as the simplified counterpart of 場, although its precise graphic route remains unresolved.
塲 is recorded as a variant form of 場.
